The status-line command string as a telemetry subject leaves: every rule confining it to diagnostics, keeping it out of home-level logs, or observing it by duration and exit only describes a surface this chunk removes; the plan names those rows as expected amendments, amended at the wrap, not in the phase.

The snapshot loses its statusline_command field, so a snapshot rebuilt by replay no longer carries it among its live fields; a snapshot or event log written by an older binary still reads (unknown fields skipped and counted, never denied), and the old-reader / new-file direction is measured at P3.

Removing the statusline-shell subject value from the diag-line schema is a schema change read against the rule that the diagnostic log schema is additive only and the rule that schema words no build can emit are removed; whether every own format's v stays 1 is the founder's fork, not decided here.

The capability ledger's two interception rows leave and relied() goes from 23 to 21; viola verify's Run B loses only its status-line probe and capture (its other pastes, probes and the claude agents --json read stay), and the start's version gate loses its statusline row group, so verify's step lines and summary count change by those rows.

The fake agent loses its StatusLine framing replay, its --settings with --statusline-stdin, the statusline-echo mode and the receipt kind statusline, and the e2e harness loses boot --statusline-echo; the removal is proved by the fake agent in CI and the code's own tests, never by a real-CLI verify in CI.

The StatusLine recorded fixtures, the claude status-line fixture schema with its hygiene validation, the two hook-stdin fuzz corpus seeds and the drift check over StatusLine variants leave; old shapes that a test must still spell live in fixture files outside the paths an identifier probe reads.

Each test case that spells the interception is sorted at P3: it leaves where it tests the interception, or is rewritten where it tests something that stays; an acceptance probe over identifiers is checked at P4 against the plan's own test cases that must spell an old word.

A guard test's one-off remove-the-guard control runs through gate.py control under a kill deadline, its case the test's name alone, holding only when that case ran and failed; no mutation run, local or dispatched.

The chrono dependency, stated as for the statusline module, leaves only if nothing else uses it; the obs plan's millisecond UTC timestamps and its direct chrono dependency for timestamps are users P3 reads before deciding.

The box-only screen fixture CARRY needs a clean viola verify --record, a live claude start: a named operator step waiting on a per-chunk cap, never planned as granted; whether --record reaches 0 fail on this account after the removal is measured at P3 without a live start or marked unmeasurable.

The live home ~/.viola/, its instance settings.json files and statusline-source.json, the pinned 0.1.0 binary and the user's ~/.claude/settings.json are not touched: no install, re-pin, or write there; a live instance keeps its own override until a named operator step re-pins it.
No code beyond the removal: no new settings, flag, env var, ledger row, log event, detail code, span or field; a later entry owns any viola-written settings for its sessions.
The cargo build and test runs research needs are each named with their wall time on a shared host, a baseline needing a build fired once, never in parallel.

viola run's start no longer reads a statusline source (the user's Claude settings statusLine or a source file), writes no instance settings override and passes no settings argument to the child; nothing is written under the Claude home or to the user's settings file.
The settings override that existed only for a plain pinned path leaves; the chunk adds no settings of its own (a later entry owns product-owned settings).

The snapshot loses its statusline_command field: a replayed snapshot still runs nothing, and a snapshot or event log written by an older binary keeps reading because viola's readers skip and count unknown fields; the old-reader direction on new files is measured.

The ledger loses the status-line override and shell rows (21 relied rows left) and viola verify's Run B loses its status-line probe settings and capture; Run B's other pastes, probes and its claude agents read stay, and verify still reads only signatures and spawns its children directly.
The version gate's statusline row group leaves; the gate still reads the stamps only through the strict-modes check.

The fake agent's StatusLine replay, settings and statusline-stdin options, statusline-echo mode and its receipt kind leave, with the harness's boot option; the remaining fake-agent seams stay behind the test-only feature and out of the release build.

The recorded StatusLine fixtures, their schema and the drift check over StatusLine variants leave; the fixture hygiene walk keeps covering every remaining recorded fixture, and no fixture is hand-written.
The hook stdin fuzz seeds for the statusline payload leave; the hook stdin parser stays in fuzz scope with its other seeds.

The log subjects of the interception leave: the diagnostics subject statusline-shell, the statusline span area, the hook statusline contract tag and the shell-spawn process-start and exit lines; the never-log floors over the statusline command lose their subject and every other never-log rule holds.
The bounded readers census loses the statusline replay read and the shell child output read; every remaining product reader stays bounded or named.
The rule that hook, MCP and statusline commands use an absolute viola path loses its statusline clause; hook and MCP commands keep it.
The chunk adds no new settings, flag, environment variable, ledger row or seam; no configuration or flag gains a way to switch a control off.
The chrono dependency leaves only if nothing else uses it; the dependency graph stays on exact pins from crates.io.

Each test case that spells the interception is sorted: it leaves if it tests the interception, or is rewritten if it tests something that stays; a rewritten case that must spell an old word keeps that word in fixture files outside the probed paths, and the retired-words fixture decides whether the removed words join it.
A guard test's one-off remove-the-guard control runs through the gate's control under a kill deadline, its case the test's name alone, and it holds only when that case ran and failed.

No install, re-pin or write under the live viola home, and no live claude start: the pinned binary and the live instances' existing overrides are untouched, and the box-only screen fixture recording is a named operator step that waits.
The version field of every own format whose field or subject is removed is not decided here: it is the founder's fork, carried with the measured compatibility facts in both directions.

viola runs no shell for any purpose: the `/bin/sh -c` status-line shell-out, its bound and its frame cap leave, and the rule that viola has no shell dependency is closed once it is gone.

The start writes no status-line override into the instance settings file, passes no settings argument for it and reads no status-line source (neither the user's settings statusLine nor a statusline source file); the plugin is still rewritten on start; the user's own settings file is never written.

The instance snapshot loses its statusline command field and every constructor literal of it; a snapshot or event log written by an older binary keeps reading because readers skip and count unknown fields, never deny them; the snapshot replay field set no longer holds the field.

The ledger loses its statusline-override and statusline-shell rows: relied rows go from 23 to 21, the version gate needs exactly the 21 relied rows, every remaining ledger row keeps its verify probe, and stamps keyed to the old ledger are read under the stamps-refuse-widened-ledger rule.

viola verify's Run B keeps its other pastes and probes and its agents listing read; only its status-line probe settings document and capture leave; whether Run B still passes a settings argument for anything else is measured.

The fake agent loses its status-line surface: the StatusLine framing replay, the settings and statusline-stdin options, the statusline-echo mode, the statusline receipt kind and its status line command execution; the harness boot loses its statusline-echo option.

The recorded StatusLine fixtures of both CLI versions, their fixture schema and its hygiene validation, and the fake agent drift check over StatusLine variants leave; every remaining CLI-version fixture set is still replayed and still matched byte for byte.
The hook stdin fuzz corpus loses its two status-line seeds; the corpus replay of that target must stay non-vacuous.

Log subjects leave: the diagnostics subject statusline-shell, the statusline span area, the contract-hook-statusline subject tag and the shell-spawn process-start and process-exit lines; diagnostics still conform to the diagnostics line schema.

Every test case that spells the interception is sorted: it leaves if it tests the interception, or is rewritten if it tests something that stays; the hook statusline test binary leaves with its manifest target and nextest filter term, and the shared helpers lose their status-line parts.
The statusline command gates (strict home, after strict modes, never over unsafe state) and the statusline settings source rules leave with the command they gated.

A guard test's one-off remove-the-guard control runs bounded under a kill deadline, its case named by the test's name alone, reaching the case past fail-fast; it holds only when that case ran and failed; no mutation run, local or dispatched.

An acceptance probe over the removed identifiers is checked against the plan's own test cases that must still spell an old word; old shapes live in fixture files outside the probed paths, and the retired-words fixture may take the removed words.
The own-format version field of the snapshot, the event log and the diagnostics line is not decided by this chunk: it is the founder's fork, laid with the measured compatibility in both directions.
